Device backups and the configuration vault

Pull configuration backups off FortiWeb and FortiADC appliances (REST or SSH), upload your own .conf files, and keep them all in one per-device vault that restore and the firmware runbook share.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsbackups.view backups.create backups.restore users.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Device Backups (URL /web/backups/<id>); also Appliances → (device) → View Backups

What is it?#

The configuration vault is SATOM's store of configuration backups, one shelf per appliance. Device Backups is the page that fills it: pull a backup off the device (over REST or SSH) or upload a .conf file you already have. The same vault is used by Configuration restore, by Upgrade Preparation and by the firmware upgrade and boot-partition runbooks, which store their safety backups here automatically.

ℹ️Note — Not the same as System Backup

This page backs up devices. Backing up SATOM itself (its database and data) is System backup.

What does it do?#

  • Lists every backup in the appliance's vault with filename, date, size, Source (Device or Upload), firmware and author. Encrypted backups carry an enc badge; a note is shown under the filename.
  • Create Backup pulls a fresh backup off the device as a background job, with a choice of transport:
Option What it does
Auto (REST → SSH) Asks the FortiWeb to create its own backup over REST and downloads it. If that fails for any reason, captures show full-configuration over SSH instead.
REST only (native device backup) Only the device's own backup; fails if the device refuses it.
SSH only (show full-configuration) Only the SSH configuration dump. Works when the REST API is locked (for example an invalid licence).
FortiADC: Auto (SSH dump) / SSH only (show full-configuration) FortiADC has no REST backup; the SSH dump is the backup.
  • Upload .conf stores a file from your computer, with an optional note.
  • Download and Delete individual backups. A download is refused if the file no longer matches the checksum recorded when it was stored.
  • Import Backup (a separate page) parses a FortiWeb configuration file offline, without touching any appliance. See below.

Requirements#

  • An appliance of kind FortiWeb or FortiADC.
  • For REST backups: a FortiWeb whose REST API answers and which has no backup password set (with a backup password the device refuses with -901; use SSH or upload).
  • For SSH backups: SSH access with the appliance's stored credentials.
  • On a multi-ADOM FortiWeb, the vault belongs to the device, not to one ADOM: one backup contains every ADOM. The page opens on the row that owns the device (see Appliances).

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the vault (the list of backups, metadata only) and the Device Backups menu entry backups.view
Create Backup, Upload .conf, Delete backups.create or backups.restore (the routes check the legacy backup key, which either one grants)
Download a backup (the full device configuration) backups.create
Import Backup page (upload, list, view) and its menu entry backups.restore
Restore a backup to a device, and the vault card on the Restore page users.manage and backups.restore (administrators). See Configuration restore.

The seeded profiles keep the access they had: read-only users hold backups.view and can now list backups; operators and administrators hold all three backups permissions.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: backups.view now opens the vault list, downloading a backup needs backups.create, and Import Backup needs backups.restore instead of any edit permission. "View Backups" for a FortiADC opened from the Global ADOM no longer ends on 404 Not Found.

🔑Permission — Without the permission

View Backups on an appliance page and the Device Backups menu entry are only shown with backups.view; without it the page answers 403 Forbidden. In the vault, Create Backup, Upload .conf and the delete icon are only shown with backups.create or backups.restore, and the download icon only with backups.create. The Import Backup menu entry is only shown with backups.restore.

How to use#

Open a device's vault#

  • From the menu: FortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Device Backups opens the vault of the device currently selected in the device picker. With no device selected you are taken to the Architecture page to pick one.
  • From an appliance: Quick Actions → View Backups (FortiWeb and FortiADC, from their own ADOM or from Global). On a multi-ADOM FortiWeb the button carries the name of the row that owns the vault, with the tooltip One backup covers every ADOM of this appliance.

Create a backup#

  1. Choose the transport in the drop-down next to Create Backup (default Auto (REST → SSH)).
  2. Click Create Backup (or Create First Backup on an empty vault).
  3. The flash says Backup started for fweb-01 — you’ll be notified when it completes (track it in the Jobs dock). The job Backup — fweb-01 shows its steps: Requesting a config backup from fweb-01…, then Downloading the configuration into the vault (…).
  4. When it finishes you get a bell notification — Backup ready: fweb-01 or Backup failed: fweb-01 — and the vault lists the new row.

A backup taken over SSH after a REST failure is stored with a note such as Captured over SSH (show full-configuration) — device REST backup unavailable (errcode -901).

Upload a backup#

  1. Click Upload .conf.
  2. Choose the Configuration file (.conf), optionally type a Note (optional), and click Store in vault.
  3. The flash confirms Stored “fweb-01.conf” in the vault (812.4 KB). (with , encrypted when the file is encrypted).

This is the reliable path when the device itself cannot produce a backup.

Download or delete#

Use the download and trash icons on a row. Deleting asks Delete backup 'fweb-01.conf' from the vault? This cannot be undone. and removes both the row and the file.

Import a backup for offline analysis#

FortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Import Backup parses a FortiWeb configuration file without contacting any appliance:

  1. Under Import a config backup, choose the Backup file (Accepted: .conf .txt .cfg .zip .gz — encrypted backups are rejected.).
  2. Optionally enter a Device name; otherwise it is taken from the configuration's hostname.
  3. Click Import. The flash reports the device, the object count and the per-section counts.
  4. Imported snapshots lists every import with device, firmware, objects, sections, source file and time. View shows the firmware, totals, Objects by section and the Raw configuration.

An imported file is not added to the vault and cannot be restored from this page; use Upload .conf for that.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Transport (Create Backup) Auto, REST only or SSH only — see above Yes (default Auto) Auto (REST → SSH)
Configuration file (.conf) File to store in the vault (.conf, .txt, .zip offered) Yes for upload fweb-01.conf
Note (optional) Free text shown under the filename No pre-migration snapshot
Backup file (Import) .conf, .txt, .cfg, .zip or .gz Yes fweb-lab.conf
Device name (Import) Folder name for the snapshot No fweb-lab

Example#

🧪Example — A licence-locked FortiWeb

fweb-03's licence expired and every REST call answers -20010.

  1. Open its vault, keep Auto (REST → SSH), click Create Backup.
  2. The REST attempt fails, the SSH dump succeeds. The new row's note reads Captured over SSH (show full-configuration) — device REST backup unavailable (errcode -20010).
  3. The backup is a plain-text configuration and can be downloaded or restored like any other.

Result#

  • A vault row with the file's size, SHA-256 checksum, encryption flag, source, firmware (when it could be read) and author; the file itself is stored on the SATOM node.
  • Audit entries: backup.create, backup.upload, backup.download, backup.delete; import_backup.create for an import.
  • Backups stored by other features appear in the same list: the pre-flight backup of Upgrade Preparation and of the firmware runbooks, the automatic pre-restore backup, the CLI capture of a Rediscovery, and uploads from the Restore page.

Troubleshooting#

"Backup failed for fweb-01: RuntimeError: REST backup failed (…); SSH fallback also failed (…). You can upload a .conf manually instead."#

Possible causes - REST: the device has a backup password set (-901), the licence is invalid (-20010), or the credentials fail. - SSH: port closed, SSH not allowed for the account, or the dump looked incomplete (SSH config dump looks truncated (missing trailing 'end') or SSH config dump looks invalid (unexpected header)).

Solution 1. Read the two reasons in the notification or on the Jobs page. 2. Fix SSH access, or remove the backup password on the device, then try again. 3. If neither is possible, export the configuration from the device GUI and use Upload .conf.

Verification — the vault lists a new row with source Device.

"device refused the backup (errcode -901): …"#

Possible causes — REST only was chosen and the FortiWeb has a backup password.

Solution — Use Auto (REST → SSH) or SSH only.

"FortiADC has no REST config-backup endpoint — use the SSH method (show full-configuration) or Auto."#

Solution — Choose Auto (SSH dump) or SSH only for FortiADC.

"Stored backup unreadable: ValueError: sha256 mismatch for fweb-01.conf — refusing to use"#

Possible causes — The file on disk changed after it was stored.

Solution — Do not use that backup; take or upload a new one.

"Choose a .conf configuration file to upload into the vault." / "The uploaded file is empty."#

Solution — Choose a non-empty file before clicking Store in vault.

"Could not import "x.conf": …"#

Possible causes — The file is encrypted, truncated, or not a FortiWeb configuration. Nothing is stored.

Solution — Import a plaintext FortiWeb backup.

"Firmware, the backup vault and the console act on the whole appliance, not on adom_a — they live on fweb-01."#

Possible causes — You opened the vault of an ADOM row of a multi-ADOM FortiWeb.

Solution — None needed: you are redirected to the device's vault.

Advanced#

Advanced Encryption detection

A backup that does not start with config or #config is treated as encrypted (a FortiWeb backup protected with a password). Encrypted backups are kept and can be restored with the backup password, but the CLI-coverage report cannot read them.

Advanced Storage

Each vault entry is a database row plus a file in its own folder under the node's data directory. Deleting the entry deletes the folder. A REST backup is created on the device, then SATOM polls the device's backup list for up to about 30 seconds before downloading it.

Advanced Scheduled backups

The scheduled action Config backup only asks the device to create a backup on the device; it does not copy it into the vault. See Scheduled actions.
